\[
e_{H,L}=\min\{1,2(|H|-1)/L\}
\]
needlessly depends on the potentially exponential number of response tables. Define the linear moment map
\[
T(q)=(r(q),s(q)).
\]
Its affine dimension is at most
\[
(|M_1|-1)+|M_1|(|M_2|-1)=m-1.
\]
Carathéodory therefore replaces every \(q\in\Delta(H)\) by a \(\bar q\) supported on at most \(m\) response tables with \(T(\bar q)=T(q)\), hence \(v(\bar q)=v(q)\). Applying the existing rounding argument to \(\bar q\) yields, at minimum,
\[
e^{\star}_{H,L}
=\min\!\left\{1,\frac{2(\min\{|H|,m\}-1)}{L}\right\},
\]
or more sharply \(2d_H/L\), where \(d_H=\operatorname{affdim}\operatorname{conv}T(H)\le m-1\). Balanced integer rounding can improve the constant further. Replacing dependence on \(|H|\) by observable dimension \(m\) is material for the advertised arbitrary-menu certification and inference, since \(|H|\) can be exponential.
